resources.string: MinkPad turns this phone into a Bluetooth keyboard, trackpad, and media remote for another device.
Keyboard and pointer input travel directly over Bluetooth. MinkPad does not save what you type.
During a session, this phone temporarily appears as Pro Controller - MinkPad followed by its usual device name. Its usual Bluetooth name returns when MinkPad closes.
Requires Android 9 or later and a phone with Bluetooth HID Device support.
Preparing the MinkPad trackpad, keyboard, and remote controls
1. Open Bluetooth settings on the device you want to control.
3. Confirm the matching pairing code on both devices.

Choose operating system or open settings
Swipe between pages or use Next. System shortcuts depend on the host and its settings.
Not mapped for this host. No command is sent.
Move one finger to move the pointer. Tap to left-click. Double-tap to double-click or select text, depending on the host app. Tap to click can be disabled in settings.
Slide one finger to move the pointer.
Two quick taps to open or highlight.
Tap with two fingers to right-click. Slide two fingers together to scroll vertically or horizontally. Invert two-finger scrolling in controller settings if the direction feels wrong.
Spread or pinch two fingers for discrete app zoom steps. This sends a keyboard shortcut, not a native trackpad pinch. Apps that do not support the shortcut will not zoom.
Hold one finger still until the small haptic tick, then move to drag. Lift to release. Double-tap and keep the second tap down also holds the left button. A host app decides what can be dragged.
Keep one finger still to hold the left button.
After holding, move the finger. Lift to drop.

Use three fingers for Back and the selected operating system’s overview shortcuts. On Mac, swipe up opens Mission Control and swipe down opens App Exposé. Some phones reserve three-finger gestures for screenshots or other system actions. Turn off Advanced host gestures in controller settings to prevent MinkPad from also sending a command. The same host actions remain available in the bottom controls.

Swipe three fingers left or right to move between Spaces and full-screen apps on Mac, or switch apps on other supported systems. Tap four fingers for the available app-list equivalent. Some host systems do not have a mapping.

Choose your receiving device’s system in controller settings. The preset is saved for that paired host; HID does not reliably reveal its operating system. Meta is Command on Apple devices and Windows on Windows. Software text uses a US layout. On a hardware-keyboard phone the live editor stays hidden; tap Type on a touch-only phone.

Start pairing opens Android’s two-minute discoverability prompt. While the countdown is running, select Pro Controller - MinkPad (your phone’s device name) in the receiving device’s Bluetooth settings and confirm the matching code. Pair new device releases the active connection before pairing another host. Android’s saved pairings are never removed automatically.

While MinkPad runs, this phone temporarily adds Pro Controller - MinkPad before its usual Bluetooth name. For example, Example Phone appears as Pro Controller - MinkPad (Example Phone). This compatibility identity gives Android receiving devices the responsive HID timing used by MinkPad. It uses the phone’s regular Bluetooth adapter, not a second custom BLE device. Existing accessory pairings are not erased, but headphones, watches, cars, and other accessories may disconnect, see the temporary name, or compete for the radio. Closing MinkPad restores the phone’s original Bluetooth name.

Open the top controls and tap the current receiving device to switch between saved devices. Starting MinkPad asks the most recently used device to reconnect. Manage saved devices includes a troubleshooting Disconnect action.

Keyboard, mouse, and media commands go directly to the receiving device. Mink does not save or upload typed text or pointer coordinates. Nearby devices access is for Bluetooth connection and discoverability, not location. Notifications provide Open, Reconnect, and Stop; denying them does not prevent input.
